neighbours.label: A determiner or possessive ('his', 'the') inside a news report of a crime or emergency (theft, assault, earthquake, fire), vs the same determiners in calm everyday or business sentences
fire: Detectives said the burglar took cash from his landlord's safe and escaped on a bicycle.
During the flood, residents were told to leave their homes and move to higher ground.
The cashier admitted stealing more than $5,000 from her former employer over two years.
Rescuers pulled two survivors from the rubble after the quake flattened the market.
Police say the gunman fired at his victims before fleeing toward the highway.
If you smell smoke in the night, crawl low to the door and feel it for heat.
The thief was caught on camera taking a laptop from the back seat of a parked car.
Witnesses said the driver abandoned his vehicle after striking the cyclist.
quiet: The gardener said the roses in his landlord's yard were blooming early this year.
During the holidays, residents were invited to decorate their homes with lanterns.
The cashier thanked her former employer for a glowing reference letter.
Shoppers filled the market after the new roof was finished last spring.
The coach praised his players before the final whistle of the friendly match.
If you wake up early, open the curtains and enjoy the morning light.
The student was seen in the library taking notes from a thick history book.
Neighbours said the driver washed his vehicle every Sunday morning.

predictions: Crime/emergency news 0.15-0.4 on 'his'/'the'; everyday or business sentences under 0.1. Weak and uneven in probes, so a fail is plausible.
notes: Card: ' his' x7, ' their', ' the' in theft from his employer, throwing his intestines, chased by his creditors, his victims; 'When' before an earthquake instruction. Probe: theft 'from his neighbor' 0.366, earthquake instruction 0.309 on ' the', firefighters 0.199; but 'attacking his wife' only 0.038, 'thanked his editor' 0.080, company profits 0.039, recipe 0.014.
